content.title: Reducers Give Complex Updates a Vocabulary
content.hook: Imagine a task application with events like:
content.context:
```text
add task
change task
remove task
mark task complete
clear completed tasks
```

If every update is handled by a different nested callback, the component can become hard to reason about.

A reducer gives those transitions names.
goals: Recognize when state transitions have become complex enough that explicit actions and a reducer make the update logic easier to reason about.

content.title: Action vocabulary

content.question: Which is the strongest benefit of action-based updates?

options.text: They make every application automatically faster.
They give complex state changes a shared vocabulary that can be inspected and reasoned about.
They remove the need for state.
They guarantee there are no bugs.

feedback.correct: A reducer does not magically remove bugs. It makes transitions explicit and centralizes the update logic.
feedback.incorrect: A reducer does not magically remove bugs. It makes transitions explicit and centralizes the update logic.

content.title: Reducer shape

feedback.correct: The reducer removes the task whose id matches the action.
feedback.incorrect: The reducer removes the task whose id matches the action.

content.title: Reducer plus context
content.text:
For a larger tree, React supports combining a reducer with context so deeply nested components can read state and dispatch actions without passing them through every intermediate component.

A useful model is:

```text
Context → shared state
Context → dispatch
Reducer → transition rules
Components → render + dispatch events
```

content.question: When is a reducer most useful?

options.text: State with many related transitions that benefit from explicit actions.

feedback.correct: A reducer earns its complexity when the transition logic benefits from being named and centralized.
feedback.incorrect: A reducer earns its complexity when the transition logic benefits from being named and centralized.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** A reducer turns “a pile of state updates” into named transitions.
**Senior habit:** When updates are getting hard to describe, write down the events first. If the event vocabulary clarifies the design, a reducer may be the right boundary.
